accepted.s: Who was the first Gupta ruler to assume the title ‘Parama Bhagavata’?
accepted.x: Chandragupta II is credited with being the first Gupta ruler to assume the title ‘Parama Bhagavata’, signifying devotion to Vishnu.
accepted.tq: Use direct ruler–title identification and distinguish closely related Gupta rulers.
accepted.sec: Gupta royal religion - religious titles → first ruler to assume (Parama Bhagavata), dynastic emblem

accepted.s: The dynastic emblem of the Guptas was represented by which of the following?
accepted.x: Garuda, the mount of Vishnu, was the royal emblem of the Gupta dynasty.
accepted.tq: Test the exact symbol–deity association rather than a general dynastic feature.
accepted.sec: Gupta royal religion - religious titles → first ruler to assume (Parama Bhagavata), dynastic emblem

accepted.s: The Garuda standard is especially found on the coins of which Gupta ruler?
accepted.x: Coins of Skandagupta carry the Garuda standard, which was the Gupta royal emblem.
accepted.tq: Apply the wrong-ruler trap by separating a dynastic emblem from the ruler whose coins display it.
accepted.sec: Gupta royal religion - religious titles → first ruler to assume (Parama Bhagavata), dynastic emblem

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Gupta religious policy:
1. The Gupta kings generally patronised Bhagavatism.
2. Samudragupta permitted Meghavarman to build a monastery at Bodh Gaya.
3. The Guptas prohibited the construction of monasteries belonging to other religions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Guptas patronised Bhagavatism, but Samudragupta also permitted Meghavarman to establish a monastery at Bodh Gaya. The claim of prohibition is false.
accepted.tq: Find the false extreme statement about religious exclusiveness.
accepted.sec: Gupta royal religion - religious titles → first ruler to assume (Parama Bhagavata), dynastic emblem

accepted.s: The Bhagavatas were the earliest devotees of which deity or divine pair?
accepted.x: The Bhagavatas were the first known worshippers of Vasudeva-Krishna. Panini also refers to the worship of Vasudeva.
accepted.tq: Use precise sect–deity matching and avoid substituting another major Hindu deity.
accepted.sec: Gupta royal religion - religious titles → first ruler to assume (Parama Bhagavata), dynastic emblem

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations best represents the principal basis of Bhagavatism under the Guptas?
o: Yoga, renunciation and ritual purity alone
accepted.x: Gupta Bhagavatism was based on Karma, Bhakti and Ahimsa.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact three-part doctrinal combination.
accepted.sec: Gupta royal religion - religious titles → first ruler to assume (Parama Bhagavata), dynastic emblem

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about Gupta-period Vaishnavism is correct?
o: It treated Garuda as a Buddhist symbol.
It preached the theory of ten incarnations of Vishnu.
It centred exclusively on fire sacrifices.
accepted.x: The avatara theory of ten incarnations of Vishnu was preached during this period.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between a positive doctrinal feature and absolute distractors.
accepted.sec: Gupta royal religion - religious titles → first ruler to assume (Parama Bhagavata), dynastic emblem

accepted.s:
Arrange the following stages of Gupta temple architecture in chronological order:
A. Deogarh and Bhitargaon temples
B. Sanchi Temple 17 and Tigawa
C. Nachna and Bhumara temples
accepted.x: The architectural sequence was first-stage Sanchi and Tigawa, second-stage Nachna and Bhumara, and third-stage Deogarh and Bhitargaon.
accepted.tq: Use the first, middle and final stages to establish the sequence.
accepted.sec: Temple plans and stages of evolution - Panchayatana layout, flat roof, shikhara beginnings, garbhagriha, mandapa

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a characteristic feature of the first stage of Gupta temple architecture?
o: Two-storeyed temple with a roofed ambulatory
Low square shikhara over the sanctum
Panchayatana plan with four corner shrines
Square sanctum, flat roof and a shallow four-pillared portico
accepted.x: The first stage, represented by Sanchi Temple 17 and Tigawa, had a square sanctum, flat roof, shallow four-pillared portico and low platform.
accepted.tq: Match the architectural stage with its defining structural features.
accepted.sec: Temple plans and stages of evolution - Panchayatana layout, flat roof, shikhara beginnings, garbhagriha, mandapa

accepted.s: Nachna and Bhumara temples are associated with which stage of temple architectural evolution?
accepted.x: Nachna and Bhumara belong to the second stage, marked by a roofed ambulatory, raised platform and two-storeyed planning.
accepted.tq: Test the example–stage association directly.
accepted.sec: Temple plans and stages of evolution - Panchayatana layout, flat roof, shikhara beginnings, garbhagriha, mandapa

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Bhitargaon is a Gupta-period Hindu temple associated with the third stage of temple evolution; it is not identified as a Buddhist chaitya in this classification.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong monument–religious structure pair among nearby architectural examples.
accepted.sec: Temple plans and stages of evolution - Panchayatana layout, flat roof, shikhara beginnings, garbhagriha, mandapa

accepted.s: The Panchayatana plan consists of:
o: Five halls arranged in a straight line
Four sanctums surrounding a central mandapa
A central shrine surrounded by four subsidiary shrines at the corners
A circular shrine with four gateways
accepted.x: In the Panchayatana layout, a main shrine is accompanied by four subsidiary shrines placed at the corners.
accepted.tq: Test the exact spatial arrangement rather than the number alone.
accepted.sec: Temple plans and stages of evolution - Panchayatana layout, flat roof, shikhara beginnings, garbhagriha, mandapa

accepted.s: Which of the following is regarded as the earliest example of the Panchayatana plan?
accepted.x: The Deogarh Dashavatara temple is regarded as the earliest example of the Panchayatana plan.
accepted.tq: Use the earliest-example trap among related Gupta temples.
accepted.sec: Temple plans and stages of evolution - Panchayatana layout, flat roof, shikhara beginnings, garbhagriha, mandapa

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the third stage of Gupta temple architecture?
o: Flat roof with a shallow four-pillared portico
Flat roof replaced by a low square shikhara and adoption of the Panchayatana plan
Exclusive use of rock-cut caves without a sanctum
Roofed ambulatory and two-storeyed sanctum without a tower
accepted.x: The third stage, represented by Deogarh and Bhitargaon, saw the disappearance of the flat roof, the emergence of a low square shikhara and the Panchayatana plan.
accepted.tq: Compare the defining transition between successive architectural stages.
accepted.sec: Temple plans and stages of evolution - Panchayatana layout, flat roof, shikhara beginnings, garbhagriha, mandapa

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT among the basic elements fixed in Gupta temple architecture?
o: Large gopura as the principal entrance tower
accepted.x: The Gupta temples established the square garbhagriha, pillared mandapa, pradakshina path and raised jagati platform. A large gopura is not listed among these basic Gupta elements.
accepted.tq: Separate the stated formative elements of Nagara architecture from a later architectural feature.
accepted.sec: Temple plans and stages of evolution - Panchayatana layout, flat roof, shikhara beginnings, garbhagriha, mandapa

accepted.s: The Gupta period is significant in temple architecture because:
o: The first free-standing Hindu temples appeared only after the Cholas.
All Gupta temples were built according to the Dravida style.
Rock-cut architecture completely disappeared during the Gupta period.
No free-standing Hindu temple survives from before the Gupta period.
accepted.x: No free-standing Hindu temple survives from a period earlier than the Guptas, making Gupta temples important in the history of structural temple architecture.
accepted.tq: Use the survival-based historical distinction without extending it into an unsupported absolute claim.
accepted.sec: Temple plans and stages of evolution - Panchayatana layout, flat roof, shikhara beginnings, garbhagriha, mandapa

accepted.s: The colossal Varaha panel at Udayagiri was carved under the patronage of:
accepted.x: The colossal Varaha panel at Udayagiri was carved under Chandragupta II, and the cave functioned as his personal temple.
accepted.tq: Apply the ruler–monument association trap.
accepted.sec: Varaha panel at Udayagiri - ruler commemorated

accepted.s: The Varaha panel at Udayagiri symbolically represents Vishnu:
o: Lifting the earth from the cosmic waters
accepted.x: The Varaha incarnation is shown lifting the earth from the sea or cosmic waters. The image was also read as symbolising the rescue of the land, possibly from the Sakas.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the correct avatara episode from other well-known mythological scenes.
accepted.sec: Varaha panel at Udayagiri - ruler commemorated

accepted.s: Who is associated with the foundation of Nalanda during the Gupta period?
accepted.x: Kumaragupta I, also known as Shakraditya, is credited with founding Nalanda.
accepted.tq: Use the founder–institution trap among Gupta rulers and Buddhist centres.
accepted.sec: Buddhism and Jainism under the Guptas - patronage evidence

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Buddhism under the Guptas:
1. Kumaragupta I founded Nalanda.
2. Samudragupta permitted Meghavarman to build a monastery at Bodh Gaya.
3. Buddhism enjoyed uninterrupted and increasing royal patronage throughout the Gupta period.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Buddhism generally lost royal patronage and declined during the Gupta period, so statement 3 is incorrect.
accepted.tq: Identify the reversal in the statement describing a long-term trend.
accepted.sec: Buddhism and Jainism under the Guptas - patronage evidence

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly explains the religious evidence associated with Udayagiri during the Gupta period?
o: One of its twenty caves was Jain.
It contained only temples dedicated to Surya.
It had no association with religious architecture.
All its caves were exclusively Buddhist.
accepted.x: Udayagiri in Madhya Pradesh has one Jain cave among its twenty caves, along with important Hindu religious sculpture.
accepted.tq: Watch for the extreme word ‘all’ in a monument-religion statement.
accepted.sec: Buddhism and Jainism under the Guptas - patronage evidence

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Scholar)
 a. Asanga
 b. Vasubandhu
 c. Dinnaga
 d. Buddhaghosa

List-II (Contribution or work)
 i. Visuddhimagga
 ii. Founder of Buddhist logic
 iii. Yogachara or Vijnanavada teacher
 iv. Abhidharmakosa

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: Asanga was a Yogachara teacher, Vasubandhu wrote the Abhidharmakosa, Dinnaga founded Buddhist logic and Buddhaghosa wrote the Visuddhimagga.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure scholar–work pairs and eliminate the remaining codes.
accepted.sec: Buddhism and Jainism under the Guptas - patronage evidence

accepted.s: Fa-Hien observed that which of the following conditions existed during his visit?
o: Mahayana and Hinayana Buddhism were both active, while some old centres had decayed.
Only Hinayana Buddhism was active in India.
The Gupta rulers had abolished Buddhist monasteries.
Jainism had completely disappeared from northern India.
accepted.x: Fa-Hien saw both Mahayana and Hinayana Buddhism active, but noted decay at Kapilavastu, Gaya and Kushinagar.
accepted.tq: Combine the traveller’s observation with the contrast between continuity and decline.
accepted.sec: Buddhism and Jainism under the Guptas - patronage evidence

accepted.s: Which Gupta-period development contributed to the decline of Buddhism?
o: Loss of royal patronage and persecution by the Huna ruler Mihirakula
A Gupta ban on all forms of image worship
The complete disappearance of Mahayana images from art
The closure of every Buddhist centre by Kumaragupta I
accepted.x: Buddhism lost royal patronage during the period, and the Huna ruler Mihirakula persecuted Buddhists. Mahayana images nevertheless flourished in Gupta art.
accepted.tq: Link the stated causes to the historical trend instead of choosing an absolute claim.
accepted.sec: Buddhism and Jainism under the Guptas - patronage evidence

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes a major religious change during the Gupta period?
o: Temple worship was replaced entirely by Vedic fire sacrifices.
Idol worship was prohibited in public temples.
Theistic and devotional Hinduism increasingly replaced sacrificial Brahmanism.
Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesh ceased to be regarded as supreme deities.
accepted.x: Hinduism became increasingly theistic and devotional, while temple-based idol worship became common and the earlier dominance of sacrificial Brahmanism declined.
accepted.tq: Choose the comprehensive description of a religious transition.
accepted.sec: Puranic Hinduism - Puranas, idol worship, temple rituals

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Moksha — one of the three components of Trivarga
accepted.x: The four Purusharthas are Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksha. The first three together are called Trivarga.
accepted.tq: Separate the threefold Trivarga from the complete fourfold Purushartha scheme.
accepted.sec: Puranic Hinduism - Puranas, idol worship, temple rituals

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Religion or tradition)
 a. Jainism
 b. Buddhism
 c. Vaishnavism
 d. Saivism

List-II (Symbol or path)
 i. Linga
 ii. Triratna
 iii. Chakra, shankha and Garuda
 iv. Ashtanga Marga

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: Jainism is associated with Triratna, Buddhism with Ashtanga Marga, Vaishnavism with chakra, shankha and Garuda, and Saivism with the linga.
accepted.tq: Begin with the distinctive symbols and then verify the associated path.
accepted.sec: Religion → founder, text, symbol, centre

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Saivism is associated with the Shiva and Kurma Puranas in the given classification, not the Arthashastra.
accepted.tq: Use the text–religion association and identify the unrelated work.
accepted.sec: Religion → founder, text, symbol, centre

accepted.s: Lakulisha is regarded as the founder of which tradition?
accepted.x: Lakulisha is identified as the founder of Saivism in its Pashupata form.
accepted.tq: Test the founder–religious tradition pair directly.
accepted.sec: Religion → founder, text, symbol, centre

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the centres listed for the major Gupta-period religions?
o: Nalanda was the principal centre of Vaishnavism, while Mathura was exclusively Buddhist.
Sarnath was identified as the principal centre of Jainism alone.
Vallabhi was the only centre of Buddhism, while Mathura was exclusively Saiva.
Mathura was associated with Vaishnavism, while Nalanda and Sarnath were Buddhist centres.
accepted.x: Mathura was associated with Vaishnavism, while Nalanda and Sarnath were important Buddhist centres. Mathura and Vallabhi were also important Jain centres.
accepted.tq: Compare the centre column across religions instead of treating each centre as exclusive.
accepted.sec: Religion → founder, text, symbol, centre

accepted.s: Nature worship is designated by which term?
accepted.x: Animism refers to the worship of nature or natural forces.
accepted.tq: Use exact terminology for a definition-based question.
accepted.sec: Religion → founder, text, symbol, centre

accepted.s: The Vallabhi council of the fifth century CE is associated with:
o: The compilation and writing down of the Svetambara canon
The composition of the Tripitaka by Buddhist monks
The foundation of Nalanda by Kumaragupta I
The beginning of the Pashupata sect
accepted.x: The Vallabhi council, held under Devarddhi Kshamashramana, compiled and committed the Svetambara Jain canon to writing.
accepted.tq: Apply the council–religious canon association.
accepted.sec: Jainism under the Guptas - Vallabhi council, Mathura school

accepted.s: Who presided over or was associated with the Vallabhi council that compiled the Svetambara canon?
accepted.x: The Vallabhi council was held under Devarddhi Kshamashramana and resulted in the compilation of the Svetambara canon.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Jain council organiser from contemporary Buddhist scholars and religious teachers.
accepted.sec: Jainism under the Guptas - Vallabhi council, Mathura school

accepted.s: Which place was a major centre of Jain art during the Gupta period, especially for images of the Tirthankaras?
accepted.x: Mathura was a major centre of Jain art, particularly for Tirthankara images.
accepted.tq: Test the centre–art tradition association directly.
accepted.sec: Jainism under the Guptas - Vallabhi council, Mathura school

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Udayagiri in Madhya Pradesh has one Jain cave among its twenty caves.
2. Fa-Hien mentions Jainism in his account.
3. Hiuen Tsang mentions Jainism in his account of the Gupta period.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Udayagiri has one Jain cave among its twenty caves, and Fa-Hien mentions Jainism. Hiuen Tsang does not mention Jainism in the stated account.
accepted.tq: Use the traveller-name distinction to detect the incorrect statement.
accepted.sec: Jainism under the Guptas - Vallabhi council, Mathura school

accepted.s: Which inscriptional evidence best illustrates the religious tolerance of the Gupta rulers?
o: Chandragupta II’s officer Amrakardava recorded a grant to a Buddhist vihara.
Samudragupta ordered the destruction of all Jain images.
Skandagupta abolished Vaishnava worship in favour of Jainism.
Kumaragupta I prohibited Buddhist institutions from receiving gifts.
accepted.x: The Sanchi inscription of Chandragupta II’s officer Amrakardava records a grant to a Buddhist vihara, demonstrating tolerance toward another faith.
accepted.tq: Identify the official, inscription and beneficiary as a linked evidence chain.
accepted.sec: Religious tolerance - Buddhist and Jain gifts in Gupta records

accepted.s: The Kahaum pillar inscription of the Skandagupta period records:
o: The construction of a Buddhist monastery by Meghavarman
The conversion of Chandragupta II to Jainism
The foundation of Nalanda by Kumaragupta I
The installation or gift of Jain images
accepted.x: The Kahaum pillar inscription of the Skandagupta period records Jain images, providing evidence of the continued presence and acceptance of Jainism.
accepted.tq: Match the inscription with its recorded religious contribution.
accepted.sec: Religious tolerance - Buddhist and Jain gifts in Gupta records

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly reflects the account of Fa-Hien concerning religious relations during the Gupta period?
o: He reported a permanent war between Hindu and Buddhist communities.
He stated that Jainism alone received state patronage.
He recorded that all Buddhist centres had disappeared.
He noted cordial relations between Hindus and Buddhists.
accepted.x: Fa-Hien noted cordial Hindu-Buddhist relations during the Gupta period, despite observing decay at certain Buddhist centres.
accepted.tq: Prefer the specific traveller observation over an extreme communal description.
accepted.sec: Religious tolerance - Buddhist and Jain gifts in Gupta records
